entry.evidence: GRACE/GRACE-FO data reveal that SVA’s annual mass-balance anomalies consistently deviate in the opposite direction from those of ACN

steps.action: Inferred regional glacier mass change for ACN and SVA (2002–2021) from GRACE/GRACE-FO Level 2 gravity fields. The method combined three SDS solutions, applied standard corrections, and used a forward-modelling inversion over glacier masks.
steps.quote: prove continuous mass loss, with rates amounting to –30.9 ± 8.3 Gt yr–1 (±2σ) in ACN

steps.action: Methods: checked the GRACE mass estimates against several references: the individual SDS solutions, an independent processing (ref. 4), CSR RL06 mascons, and a bootstrap over months. These checks also gave the uncertainty budget.
steps.quote: yields annual rates that differ from our estimates within ±4 Gt yr–1 for ACN and ±5 Gt yr–1 for SVA

steps.action: Observed that detrended annual (March-to-March) GRACE mass-balance anomalies of SVA and ACN have opposite signs in all but two of 17 balance periods.
steps.quote: only two years are exceptions from this counter-directional mass-balance behaviour

steps.action: Asked whether the counter-directional behaviour also holds before the GRACE era.
steps.quote: [...] the same characteristics hold true for the time before the GRACE/GRACE-FO era

steps.action: Reconstructed the 1950–2019 SMB of both regions with the regional climate model MAR3.11 forced six-hourly by ERA5 at 15 km resolution.
steps.quote: [...] SMB of the two regions using the regional climate model MAR3.11 (1950–2019)

steps.action: Compared cumulative monthly MAR3.11 SMB-D* with the GRACE/GRACE-FO series over their common period; the model lies typically within 2σ.
steps.quote: Cumulative monthly SMB from MAR3.11 typically lies within 2σ error margins of the GRACE/GRACE-FO time series

steps.action: Methods/Extended Data: compared alternative SMB models (MAR3.11 forced by NCEP/NCAR; RACMO2.3p1) with the ERA5-forced MAR3.11 output and GRACE. Both gave similar results; ERA5-forced MAR was retained as the best fit.
steps.quote: Simulations based on the regional climate model RACMO2p121 for 1958–2015 are consistent with MAR3.11 output using ERA5

steps.action: Estimated constant discharge D* as the difference between the GRACE and SMB trends, allowing for a cited Austfonna surge loss. They subtracted D* back to 1950, detrended with a cubic polynomial, and derived annual balance anomalies.
steps.quote: we detrend the monthly time series for the entire period 1950–2019 using a polynomial fit (order n = 3)

steps.action: Established from the 1950–2019 reconstruction that the relation between the regions shifted over time. Phases of same-sign and opposite-sign behaviour alternate, and 15-yr running correlations become significantly negative (< –0.7) from 1999–2013.
steps.quote: pointing to a new state of atmospheric forcing conditions

steps.action: Designed a categorization of years into four sign classes (+|+, –|–, +|–, –|+) counted in running 15-yr bins, matching the span of the first GRACE mission.
steps.quote: we categorize the yearly mass-balance anomalies of ACN and SVA into four types on the basis of their sign and synchronicity

steps.action: Selected the most synchronous (1963–1977) and most asynchronous (2004–2018) periods from the record. They restricted the analysis to JJA because melt dominates interannual variability (Extended Data Fig. 3), using z500, northward heat flux and t2m from reanalyses.
steps.quote: We analyse the atmospheric conditions in years with dominantly synchronous (1963–1977) and asynchronous (2004–2018) mass-balance behaviour

steps.action: Compared maps of z500 correlation with mass balance between the two periods. Correlations peak over each region early on; later they form nearly complementary patterns that flank the regions.
steps.quote: the correlations for ACN and SVA reveal nearly complementary patterns for both regions

steps.action: Repeated the 2004–2018 correlation analysis with GRACE/GRACE-FO mass balances instead of modelled SMB, obtaining consistent patterns (Extended Data Fig. 5).
steps.quote: Employing GRACE/GRACE-FO mass-balance anomalies instead of SMB anomalies for 2004–2018 produces very consistent correlation patterns

steps.action: Methods: checked the consistency of the ERA20C and ERA5 heat-flux correlations over the 1979–1995 overlap before splicing the two reanalyses.
steps.quote: The resulting standard deviation of the difference of the correlation coefficients is <0.05 in both cases, indicating acceptable consistency between datasets

steps.action: Compared correlations with vertically integrated northward heat flux between periods. Two distinct, alternating heat-transport channels appear only in recent years.
steps.quote: The correlation patterns confirm two distinct channels of heat transport to govern the recent mass-balance years

steps.action: Drew 5,000 random samples of annual SMB anomalies under the empirically estimated SMB uncertainties (§7.6) to infer, for each 15-yr bin, the probability of an asynchronous majority. Asynchrony is very likely from the bin centred on 2004, and exceeding 2011 levels stays below 5% earlier (Extended Data Figs. 6–7).
steps.quote: Starting in the early 2000s, asynchronous behaviour has become very likely (following the IPCC definitions28)

steps.action: Formed JJA composites of z500 and 250 hPa wind for same-sign versus opposite-sign years. Same-sign years show zonal, circumpolar flow; opposite-sign years show a planetary wave pattern with meridional flow.
steps.quote: the composite difference of opposite-sign years depicts a wave pattern of z500 anomalies across the Arctic domain

steps.action: Propagated categorization uncertainty from the SMB ensemble into the z500 composites (Extended Data Fig. 10).
steps.quote: The uncertainties in the z500 composites arising from uncertainties in the SMB reconstruction are presented in Extended Data Fig. 10.

steps.action: Kept the claim that meridional-circulation years have superseded zonal ones since the late 1990s and increasingly control the mass balance of both regions.
steps.quote: The occurrence of years associated with zonal circulation drops from roughly 73% in the time frame 1963–1977 to only 20% during 2004–2018

steps.action: Placed the asynchrony in the published 'new Arctic' picture of quasi-stationary planetary waves and Greenland blocking. Other factors (NAO non-stationarity, synoptic variance, natural versus anthropogenic causes) are named but not tested.
steps.quote: in line with a statistically significant increase of quasi-stationary planetary wave patterns29

end.claim: From 1950 to 2019, glacier mass balances in Svalbard and northern Arctic Canada have become very likely asynchronous since the early 2000s, beyond earlier decadal variability, in association with more frequent meridional (wavier) summer circulation and heat advection.

decisive_move.sentence: The MAR3.11 SMB reconstruction back to 1950 supplies the pre-GRACE baseline. Without it the GRACE-era asynchrony could not be shown to exceed previous decadal variability, and the period comparison of circulation would be impossible.

gates.evidence: The data (GRACE, MAR3.11 output, reanalyses) were not acquired under a stated hypothesis; the MAR extension answers a question raised by the GRACE observation (§2 ¶3). The asynchrony claim faced tests it could have failed: the Monte Carlo SMB-uncertainty ensemble could have shown no dominant category, and the correlation patterns could have differed when GRACE replaced the modelled SMB (§4 ¶2, §4 ¶4). The circulation interpretation was not tested against stated rivals. Analysis periods, bin width and detrending order were chosen after inspecting the record, and nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: Monte Carlo random sampling (N = 5,000) of uncertain annual anomalies to obtain category probabilities
Student's t test with autocorrelation-reduced degrees of freedom for correlation significance

limits: No peer-review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded; the reviewers are only named (Additional information, PDF p. 10). Coding the entry as an anomaly is inference: the paper never calls the GRACE counter-phase surprising, and the abstract frames the work as using glaciers to categorize circulation. No rival explanations are posed or tested. The mechanism (meridional heat advection, blocking, planetary waves) is a sub-claim at best_explanation status at most, supported by correlation and composite patterns and consistency with cited work (§6 ¶3). The probability that asynchrony is very likely since the early 2000s is a sub-claim at estimate_with_resolution, conditional on the empirically derived SMB uncertainty (§7.6 ¶1), which itself uses GRACE. The paper does not say whether the periods 1963–1977 and 2004–2018, the 15-yr bin width or the cubic detrending order were fixed before the data were inspected; inference suggests they were chosen post hoc from Fig. 2b. Supplementary Table 1 (zonal-year percentages) was not supplied. The paper makes no explicit 'first' or 'previously unknown' statements. The Monte Carlo ensemble is coded as I (estimation) per codebook section 3, and it is also listed as a robustness check in v_checks. Triangulation (computed): replication (GRACE-based correlations) plus method checks (independent GRACE processing, mascons, RACMO).

disagreements.target: Global climate models and projections of the Arctic (refs 31, 38, including CMIP6 blocking projections)
disagreements.support: The observed shift to meridional circulation found here, together with cited model evaluations, implies that projections missing these dynamics may underestimate impacts.
disagreements.quote: To date, global models fail to reproduce the observed atmospheric characteristics of the new Arctic31,38.
